objective: Prove the relay CARRIES the cross-mesh write when there is no direct path — forced purely via iroh address config (relay-only EndpointAddr), NO Docker, NO firewall, NO killing nodes (the POC-3 confound).
mechanism: RAFKA_FORCE_RELAY=1 makes a node advertise a RELAY-ONLY location (its relay URL, no direct addr) in its gossiped digest; the gateway dials the cross-mesh target via EndpointAddr::new(id).with_relay_url(url) (no direct addr). RAFKA_RELAY_URL points at a locally-run iroh-relay (E:/iroh/iroh-relay; iroh/docs/local_relays.md). Default off = sprint-14 direct behavior.
acceptance_tests: T1 BUILD: `cargo check --workspace --tests --no-default-features` = 0 errors, 0 new warnings.

T2 RELAY-ONLY ADDR (curl): with RAFKA_FORCE_RELAY=1, `GET /api/topology-cache` shows the target broker's `location` is the RELAY URL (or empty/relay-marked) — NOT a 127.0.0.1 loopback addr. With FORCE off, it IS a loopback addr.

T3 DELIVERY VIA RELAY (curl, measured): with FORCE_RELAY=1 + a running iroh-relay, the cross-mesh target broker's `frames_recv_total` (via /api/heartbeats) CLIMBS over a 60s window — the write lands with NO direct path available.
T4 RELAY NOT IDLE (observable): the iroh-relay shows it carried traffic (relay process log line / metric / a span attribute path=relay) — distinct from sprint-14 where the relay was idle.
T5 NO-CONFOUND (code): relay is forced ONLY via address/relay config; grep proves no node is killed to force relay, no firewall call, no Docker.
T6 TOGGLE-OFF (curl): with RAFKA_FORCE_RELAY unset, the same write goes DIRECT (target location is loopback) — no regression to sprint-14.
proof_required: Jaeger trace of a forced-relay cross-mesh write; the curl outputs for T2/T3/T6 saved as .json; relay-active evidence for T4. Screenshots into docs/plans/mesh-v2/verify/screenshots/sprint16-forced-relay/.
out_of_scope: multi-relay, relay failover, real cross-host NAT, app-layer/partition concepts

ports.note: fresh; leave other instances up; RAFKA_MDNS_ENABLE=false
